description: Standard carbon structural steel widely utilized for riveted, bolted, or welded construction of buildings, bridges, and general structural components.

C.note: Max for plates <= 0.75 in [20 mm]. Thicknesses > 0.75 to 1.5 in allow 0.26%; > 1.5 to 4 in allow 0.27%.

Mn.note: Applies to plates over 0.75 in [20 mm] thickness; no Mn requirement for thinner plates.

Si.note: Mandatory only for plates over 1.5 in [40 mm] thickness.

Cu.note: Only required when copper-bearing steel is specified.

yield_strength.condition: As-rolled, structural plates <= 8 in [200 mm] and shapes

tensile_strength.condition: As-rolled standard room temperature tensile specimen

elongation_pct.gauge_length: 8 in [200 mm] (23% min in 2 in [50 mm])

charpy_impact.note: Optional supplementary requirement S5; not guaranteed in basic standard.

typical_uses: Commercial building frame columns and girders
Base plates, gussets, and anchor brackets
Equipment skids and agricultural frames
Storage tanks and non-pressure vessel enclosures

environmental_suitability.indoor_dry: Excellent performance with standard shop primer.
environmental_suitability.outdoor_atmospheric: Requires durable primer and topcoat or hot-dip galvanizing to prevent uniform rusting.
environmental_suitability.marine_offshore: Unsuitable without barrier coatings or cathodic protection.
environmental_suitability.sub_zero: Not recommended for dynamic sub-zero service (-20°F or below) without supplementary CVN impact testing.
environmental_suitability.high_temperature: Design allowable stress decreases rapidly above 650°F [345°C].

corrosion_resistance.details: Plain carbon steel with no passive chromium film. Typical unpainted corrosion rate in mild industrial atmospheres is 20-50 µm/year.

weldability.notes: Prequalified under AWS D1.1 Group I. Low carbon equivalent (<0.40 CEV typical). Preheat only needed for thick plates (>1.5 in) or ambient temp below 32°F [0°C].

known_limitations: Wide allowable tensile range (58-80 ksi) results in heat-to-heat yield variation.
Charpy V-notch toughness is not mandatory under standard specification.
Uncontrolled yield-to-tensile ratio limits use in high-seismic moment frames without AISC 341 testing.
avoid_for: Unpainted marine atmospheric exposure
Sub-zero dynamic impact applications without Supplementary S5 impact test
Sour gas (H2S) service (NACE MR0175 compliance required)

cross_standard_equivalents.source_notes: Minimum yield is 275 MPa (39.9 ksi), slightly higher than A36; chemistry and weldability align closely.
Tensile range 400-510 MPa matches; SS400 does not specify chemical limits except P and S.
Canadian standard weldable grade with minimum 260 MPa (37.7 ksi) yield.

description: Columbium-vanadium micro-alloyed structural steel offering superior strength-to-weight ratio and excellent weldability for bridges and construction equipment.

C.note: Max for plates up to 4 in [100 mm] thickness.

Mn.note: Plates up to 1.5 in allow 1.35% max; shapes up to 1.60% max.

Si.note: For plates over 1.5 in, Si minimum 0.15% is required.

Nb.note: Columbium (Niobium) for grain refinement and precipitation hardening.

yield_strength.condition: As-rolled, plates <= 4 in [100 mm] and structural shapes

tensile_strength.condition: Standard room temperature test per ASTM A6/A6M

elongation_pct.gauge_length: 8 in [200 mm] (21% min in 2 in [50 mm])

charpy_impact.note: AASHTO Zone 2 toughness typically ordered via Supplementary S5.

typical_uses: Highway bridges and rail overpasses
Heavy mobile crane booms and outriggers
High-rise commercial building columns
Electrical transmission towers and utility poles

environmental_suitability.outdoor_atmospheric: Requires protective paint, hot-dip galvanizing, or metallizing.
environmental_suitability.marine_offshore: Requires heavy epoxy barrier coatings or sacrificial anodes.
environmental_suitability.sub_zero: Reliable down to -20°F when ordered with Charpy Supplementary S5 impact requirements.
environmental_suitability.high_temperature: Creep and yield strength reduction begins above 650°F [345°C].

corrosion_resistance.details: Corrosion rate comparable to plain carbon steel. Microalloying additions (V/Nb) do not enhance atmospheric corrosion resistance.

weldability.notes: Prequalified under AWS D1.1 Group II. Low hydrogen electrodes (E7018) recommended. Typical CEV is 0.38-0.44.

relative_cost_tier.description: Modest premium over A36 with 38% higher yield strength.

known_limitations: Plate thickness limited to 4 in [100 mm] for Grade 50 under standard specification.

avoid_for: Uncoated weathering applications (use A588 instead)
Wear-abrasion chutes (use AR400 or A514 instead)

cross_standard_equivalents.source_notes: Minimum yield 355 MPa (51.5 ksi) closely matches A572-50. S355J2 includes verified -20°C impact toughness.
Standard Canadian 350 MPa yield weldable grade.

description: High-strength low-alloy structural steel with enhanced atmospheric corrosion resistance (Corten-type), forming a protective, self-passivating oxide patina.

C.note: Max ladle analysis for Grade A.

Mn.note: Essential for strength and toughness balance.

Cr.note: Key alloying element for protective rust layer.

Ni.note: Grade A allows up to 0.40% max.

Cu.note: Crucial element promoting dense adherence of oxide layer.

chemistry_limits.source: ASTM A588/A588M-19 Table 1 Chemical Requirements for Grade A

yield_strength.condition: As-rolled, plates <= 4 in [100 mm] (46 ksi for 4-5 in, 42 ksi for 5-8 in)

tensile_strength.condition: Plates up to 4 in [100 mm] thickness

elongation_pct.gauge_length: 8 in [200 mm] (21% min in 2 in [50 mm])

charpy_impact.note: Bridge structures typically specify AASHTO Zone 2 fracture-critical CVN.

typical_uses: Unpainted highway bridge girders and trusses
Architectural facades and sculptural structures
Transmission towers and telecommunications poles
Rail freight hopper cars

environmental_suitability.indoor_dry: Patina will not develop; requires alternating wet-dry outdoor cycles to form protective oxide.
environmental_suitability.outdoor_atmospheric: Excellent in rural, urban, and moderate industrial climates with cyclical wet-dry conditions.
environmental_suitability.marine_offshore: Not recommended within 0.5 miles of saltwater surf; airborne chlorides prevent stable patina formation.
environmental_suitability.sub_zero: Good sub-zero toughness when ordered to AASHTO M270 Grade 50W impact specs.

corrosion_resistance.details: ASTM G101 atmospheric corrosion index >= 6.0, providing approximately 4x greater atmospheric corrosion resistance than plain carbon steel when exposed unpainted to cyclical weather.

weldability.notes: Prequalified under AWS D1.1 Group II. Weathering matching electrodes (e.g., E8018-W2) must be used to ensure weld deposit matches base metal patina color and corrosion resistance.

relative_cost_tier.description: Higher initial material cost offset by total elimination of initial painting and maintenance repainting.

known_limitations: Requires alternating wet and dry environmental cycles to form adherent patina; continuously wet or buried steel will corrode like carbon steel.
Initial rust runoff during the first 2-5 years can stain underlying concrete abutments.
Yield strength drops for thicknesses > 4 in [100 mm].
avoid_for: Marine coastal environments subject to ocean spray (< 0.5 mi from breaking surf)
Buried applications or submerged service
Sheltered architectural pockets where moisture and debris accumulate permanently

cross_standard_equivalents.source_notes: European standard weathering steel with 355 MPa yield and -20°C CVN impact guarantee.
Highway bridge specification matching A588 chemistry with mandatory CVN testing.

description: General-purpose low-carbon machinery steel offering excellent machinability, cold formability, case-hardening capability, and easy weldability.

C.note: Narrow carbon range ensures predictable response to carburizing.

P.note: Max ladle analysis for standard carbon steel.

chemistry_limits.source: SAE J403 / ASTM A29 Table 1 Chemical Composition

yield_strength.condition: Cold drawn bar <= 0.75 in per ASTM A108 (Hot rolled typical is 32 ksi min)

tensile_strength.condition: Cold drawn bar condition per ASTM A108 (Hot rolled typical is 58 ksi)

charpy_impact.note: Not governed by ASTM A108 / SAE J403 specification; dependent on cold reduction.

typical_uses: Pins, studs, bolts, and threaded fasteners
Carburized gears, ratchets, and camshafts
Hydraulic fittings and cylindrical bushings
Precision machined fixture tooling and sprockets

environmental_suitability.indoor_dry: Requires light rust preventive oil during transit and storage.
environmental_suitability.outdoor_atmospheric: Requires zinc plating, black oxide with oil, or painting.
environmental_suitability.marine_offshore: Rapid rusting unless nickel/chrome plated or stainless substituted.
environmental_suitability.sub_zero: Transition temperature is relatively high; not suitable for low-temperature impact service.
environmental_suitability.high_temperature: Not intended for sustained elevated temperatures above 600°F [315°C].

corrosion_resistance.details: Plain mild engineering carbon steel with zero passive resistance.

weldability.notes: Low carbon content minimizes hardening during welding. Does not require preheat or postweld heat treatment in typical section thicknesses.

relative_cost_tier.description: Inexpensive precision bar stock with modest cold-drawing processing adder.

known_limitations: Through-hardening is impossible due to low carbon (0.20% max); surface hardness requires case carburizing.
Mechanical properties depend entirely on cold work; hot-rolled material has much lower yield strength (~32 ksi).
avoid_for: Heavy shock-loaded shafts requiring core hardness > 30 HRC
Direct through-hardened tooling (use 4140 or 1045 instead)
Corrosive chemical environments

cross_standard_equivalents.source_notes: European case-hardening carbon steel with 0.12-0.18% C.
Japanese standard carbon steel with 0.13-0.18% C.

description: Medium-carbon engineering steel offering good strength, moderate hardenability, wear resistance, and heat treatability (quench and temper or flame/induction hardening).

C.note: Provides sufficient carbon for 50-55 HRC surface induction hardening.

yield_strength.condition: As-rolled hot rolled bar (Normalized is ~54 ksi, Q&T can achieve 75-100 ksi)

tensile_strength.condition: Hot rolled bar condition per ASTM A29

charpy_impact.note: Medium carbon steels exhibit ductile-to-brittle transition near ambient temperature.

typical_uses: Power transmission shafts, axles, and spindles
Induction-hardened hydraulic cylinder rods
Forged crankshafts and heavy connecting rods
Gears, guide pins, and high-tensile bolts

environmental_suitability.indoor_dry: Requires corrosion preventive oil or hard chrome plating on rods.
environmental_suitability.outdoor_atmospheric: Requires protective plating (electroless nickel, hard chrome) or paint.
environmental_suitability.marine_offshore: Prone to severe pitting and crevice corrosion without specialized seal coatings.
environmental_suitability.sub_zero: Low notch toughness at cold temperatures.

corrosion_resistance.details: Plain medium-carbon steel lacking chromium or nickel passivating elements.

weldability.notes: Higher carbon content (0.43-0.50% C) produces high risk of hard, brittle martensitic HAZ and hydrogen cracking. Preheat to 300-500°F [150-260°C] and low-hydrogen electrodes mandatory.

known_limitations: Poor weldability compared to mild steel; requires strict preheat and interpass thermal management.
Shallow hardenability in large diameters (>2.5 in) during oil quench; water quench risks distortion or quench cracking.
avoid_for: Complex welded structural fabrications
Large diameter (>3 in) through-hardened shafts (use alloy 4140 instead)
Severe cyclic impact at low temperatures

cross_standard_equivalents.source_notes: European standard 0.45% carbon engineering steel.

description: Versatile chromium-molybdenum alloy steel with high hardenability, good fatigue strength, excellent torsional strength, and shock resistance.

C.note: Carbon content balances core toughness and high hardened tensile strength.

Cr.note: Chromium provides deep hardenability and temper resistance.

Mo.note: Molybdenum prevents temper embrittlement and enhances elevated temp strength.

chemistry_limits.source: ASTM A29/A29M Table 1 and SAE J404 Table 1

yield_strength.condition: Quenched & tempered / prehardened condition (28-32 HRC, e.g. ASTM A193 B7)

tensile_strength.condition: Quenched & tempered bar up to 2.5 in diameter

charpy_impact.note: Achievable in properly vacuum-degassed Q&T condition.

typical_uses: Oil & gas downhole drill collars, pup joints, and tool bodies
High-pressure studs and bolting (ASTM A193 Grade B7)
Heavy automotive drive axles, steering knuckles, and crankshafts
Machine tool spindle gears and extrusion press rams

environmental_suitability.outdoor_atmospheric: Requires barrier coating or plating (phosphate, cadmium alternative, zinc-nickel).
environmental_suitability.marine_offshore: Requires NACE MR0175 / ISO 15156 hardness restriction (max 22 HRC) if exposed to H2S sour gas environments.
environmental_suitability.sub_zero: Good impact toughness at -40°F when properly tempered.
environmental_suitability.high_temperature: Creep resistant up to 900°F [480°C] due to molybdenum content.

corrosion_resistance.details: Low-alloy steel with ~1% Cr; does not form a passive protective film.

weldability.notes: High hardenability (CEV ~0.70). High susceptibility to cold cracking. Mandatory preheat 400-600°F [200-315°C], low hydrogen consumables, and immediate postweld stress relief or temper.

relative_cost_tier.description: Premium alloy machinery steel reflecting Cr-Mo alloying and precision heat treatment.

known_limitations: Highly prone to hydrogen-induced underbead cracking during field welding.
Susceptible to sulfide stress cracking in sour service unless hardness is kept below 22 HRC per NACE MR0175.
avoid_for: Field welding without specialized thermal preheat and post-weld stress relief equipment
Corrosive acid or saltwater exposure without protective cladding

cross_standard_equivalents.source_notes: European standard 42CrMo4 with virtually identical chemical and mechanical limits.
Standard Japanese chromium-molybdenum machinery grade.

description: The classic 18/8 austenitic stainless steel with excellent general corrosion resistance, high formability, ductility, and cryogenic toughness.

C.note: ASTM A240 limits C to 0.07% max (was 0.08% in older revisions).

Cr.note: Provides passive self-healing chromium oxide film.

yield_strength.condition: Annealed sheet, strip, and plate per ASTM A240

charpy_impact.note: Austenitic face-centered cubic structure maintains impact toughness down to liquid nitrogen temps.

typical_uses: Food and dairy processing tanks and piping
Commercial kitchen equipment and sinks
Architectural panels and exterior trim
Cryogenic storage vessels and cold-boxes

environmental_suitability.outdoor_atmospheric: Excellent in urban and rural atmospheres; may experience brown tea-staining in marine coastal air.
environmental_suitability.marine_offshore: Susceptible to chloride crevice corrosion and pitting; 316L or duplex preferred.
environmental_suitability.sub_zero: Superb cryogenic ductility down to -320°F [-196°C] without brittle transition.
environmental_suitability.high_temperature: Resists scaling up to 1600°F [870°C] intermittent service.

corrosion_resistance.details: Resistant to oxidizing acids (nitric acid) and organic food acids. PREN is approximately 18.0-19.5.

weldability.notes: Readily weldable using AWS ER308 filler. In heavy welded sections, risk of chromium carbide precipitation at grain boundaries (sensitization); use low-carbon 304L for thick as-welded assemblies.

relative_cost_tier.description: High material cost due to 8-10.5% nickel and 18% chromium content.

known_limitations: Susceptible to chloride stress corrosion cracking (CSCC) above 140°F [60°C].
Sensitization risk during welding or slow cooling between 800-1500°F [425-815°C] in standard carbon (non-L) grade.
avoid_for: Warm chlorinated water or swimming pool environments (risk of sudden CSCC failure)
Seawater immersion without cathodic protection
Welded components exposed to corrosive media without post-weld solution annealing (use 304L instead)

cross_standard_equivalents.source_notes: European standard 1.4301 corresponds directly to AISI 304.
Standard Japanese 18-8 austenitic stainless steel.

description: Extra-low carbon molybdenum-bearing austenitic stainless steel providing superior resistance to pitting, crevice corrosion, and sensitization in chloride environments.

C.note: Low carbon prevents chromium carbide sensitization during welding.

Ni.note: Higher nickel stabilizes austenite in presence of molybdenum.

Mo.note: Molybdenum provides enhanced resistance to chloride pitting.

yield_strength.condition: Annealed sheet and plate per ASTM A240 (170 MPa min)

tensile_strength.condition: Annealed condition per ASTM A240 (485 MPa min)

charpy_impact.note: Superior cryogenic notch toughness down to liquid helium temperatures.

typical_uses: Marine hardware, offshore rig piping, and boat fittings
Pharmaceutical batch reactors and sterile biotechnology piping
Chemical processing tanks handling organic and sulfuric acids
Flue gas desulfurization (FGD) scrubbers and marine exhaust scrubbers

environmental_suitability.outdoor_atmospheric: Impervious to industrial smog and coastal marine atmospheric tea-staining.
environmental_suitability.marine_offshore: Excellent in marine atmospheres and splash zones (though stagnant seawater requires duplex or 6-Mo).
environmental_suitability.sub_zero: Outstanding cryogenic service capability down to -320°F [-196°C].
environmental_suitability.high_temperature: Continuous service up to 1500°F [815°C]; low carbon avoids sensitization.

corrosion_resistance.details: PREN calculation: Cr + 3.3(Mo) + 16(N) = ~23.1 to 25.0. Significantly outperforms 304 in chlorides, de-icing salts, and acidic environments.

weldability.notes: Welds easily with AWS ER316L filler. The 0.030% max carbon eliminates knife-line intergranular corrosion without requiring postweld solution annealing.

relative_cost_tier.description: Substantial cost premium reflecting 2-3% molybdenum and 10-14% nickel.

known_limitations: Susceptible to chloride stress corrosion cracking above 140°F [60°C] under tensile stress.
Relatively low minimum yield strength (25 ksi per ASTM A240) in annealed condition.
Crevice corrosion can occur under bio-fouling or gaskets in warm stagnant seawater.
avoid_for: Warm stagnant seawater piping (use Duplex 2205 or Super Duplex 2507 instead)
Hot concentrated hydrochloric acid service

cross_standard_equivalents.source_notes: European standard 1.4404 matches AISI 316L in composition and performance.
Standard Japanese low-carbon 316 grade.

description: Titanium-stabilized 11% chromium ferritic stainless steel providing heat and oxidation resistance at high temperatures, widely used in automotive exhaust systems.

C.note: Low carbon per modern ASTM A240 revisions.

Cr.note: Entry level chromium content for stainless passivation.

Ti.note: Titanium stabilization formula: min 6x(C+N) or 0.15% min, max 0.75%.

yield_strength.condition: Annealed condition per ASTM A240 (205 MPa min)

tensile_strength.condition: Annealed condition per ASTM A240 (380 MPa min)

charpy_impact.note: Ferritic stainless undergoes ductile-to-brittle transition near 32°F [0°C]; not rated for cryogenic impact.

typical_uses: Automotive exhaust pipes, mufflers, and catalytic converter shells
Agricultural fertilizer spreaders and grain dry chutes
Industrial furnace flue boxes and heat exchangers
Culvert pipe liners and bus structural frames

environmental_suitability.outdoor_atmospheric: Forms a superficial cosmetic brown surface discoloration (tea staining), but resists perforation.
environmental_suitability.marine_offshore: Unsuitable for aesthetic or severe salt spray applications.
environmental_suitability.sub_zero: Poor low-temperature impact toughness; exhibits room-temperature DBTT transition.
environmental_suitability.high_temperature: Resists scaling and oxidation up to 1250°F [675°C] continuous (1400°F [760°C] intermittent).

corrosion_resistance.details: Sufficient chromium to resist hot exhaust gas condensate corrosion and atmospheric rust-through, but will discolor on surface. PREN ~11.0.

weldability.notes: Weldable with ER409 or ER309 filler. Excessive heat input causes rapid grain coarsening in the HAZ, leading to reduced toughness. Titanium stabilization prevents sensitization.

relative_cost_tier.description: Economical stainless steel due to absence of expensive nickel and molybdenum.

known_limitations: Develops superficial cosmetic rust staining in outdoor atmospheres.
HAZ grain coarsening limits weld joint toughness in heavy sections (>0.125 in).
Brittle at sub-zero temperatures.
avoid_for: Decorative architectural surfaces where visual appearance matters (use 304 or 316 instead)
Food contact surfaces or sterile pharmaceutical equipment
Cryogenic storage tanks

description: Austenitic-ferritic (50/50 phase balance) duplex stainless steel combining approximately twice the yield strength of 300-series stainless with outstanding resistance to chloride stress corrosion cracking.

C.note: Low carbon prevents intergranular carbide precipitation.

Cr.note: UNS S32205 restricts Cr to 22.0-23.0% (S31803 allows 21.0-23.0%).

Mo.note: UNS S32205 restricts Mo to 3.0-3.5% (S31803 allows 2.5-3.5%).

N.note: Nitrogen boosts PREN and ensures rapid austenite reformation during welding cooling.

chemistry_limits.source: ASTM A240/A240M-22a Table 1 for UNS S32205

yield_strength.condition: Annealed sheet and plate per ASTM A240 (450 MPa min, >2x AISI 304/316)

charpy_impact.note: Standard specification guarantees good impact toughness down to -40°F [-40°C].

typical_uses: Offshore oil & gas separation vessels, piping, and manifolds
Chemical cargo tanks for marine product tankers
Pulp & paper bleach plant digesters and liquor tanks
Reverse osmosis seawater desalination pressure vessels and pumps

environmental_suitability.indoor_dry: Superb, high strength allows thinner wall sections.
environmental_suitability.outdoor_atmospheric: Completely immune to coastal and industrial atmospheric staining.
environmental_suitability.marine_offshore: Outstanding resistance to seawater splash zones, salt spray, and brackish brine.
environmental_suitability.sub_zero: Rated down to -40°F [-40°C]; below -50°F ferrite phase suffers ductile-to-brittle transition.
environmental_suitability.high_temperature: Restricted to maximum 572°F [300°C] continuous due to risk of 475°C [885°F] embrittlement and sigma phase.

corrosion_resistance.details: PREN: Cr + 3.3(Mo) + 16(N) = 34.0 to 36.0. High resistance to chloride stress corrosion cracking, erosion-corrosion, and pitting.

weldability.rating: Good (Requires Controlled Heat Input & Phase Balance)

avoid_for: High-temperature service exceeding 572°F [300°C] (risk of sigma phase embrittlement)
Cryogenic service below -40°F [-40°C] (use 304L or 316L instead)
